evidence.curator_note: Equation 4.28 is a chemical-ionization (CI) pathway: R-OH is first protonated by the CI reagent to the even-electron ion R-OH2(+) (first arrow, labelled 'H+ / Cl' as a reagent arrow with 0 fishhook arcs drawn), which then undergoes inductive cleavage (arrow 'i') to R(+) + H2O. Only the inductive-cleavage step is encoded here as an electron-pushing step: the R-O sigma bond breaks heterolytically with both electrons going to oxygen, giving neutral water and R(+). Book draws 1 arc for this step (a single full curved arrow from the R-O bond onto O); move 1 (electron_count 2) is that drawn arrow. The protonation step is NOT encoded as a formal_arrow_step -- it is a reagent association (0 arcs) and the transferred/hydroxyl H atoms cannot be carried as mapped atoms because RDKit absorbs explicit mapped H into implicit counts. Instantiated as protonated methanol CH3-OH2(+) (R=CH3), MH+ m/z 33.0335; R(+) computed m/z 15.0229 derives from R=CH3, not the book (no m/z or % printed on this generic scheme). Text: (M+H-H2O)+ at m/z 148 for ephedrine is the concrete manifestation the book cites.

Cross-linked MØD rules. IMS_4_28_2 ([_A]1[O+]2([H]3)([H]4) >> [_A+]1.[O]2([H]3)([H]4)) MATCHES step_inductive_cleavage: it cleaves the R-O bond, sends both electrons to O and expels neutral H2O leaving R(+); this rule is correct and bond-order/electron conserving (water has no internal multiple bond to drop, unlike the CO/CH2O neutrals of 4_27_2 / 4_26_2). IMS_4_28_1 ([_A]1[O]2[H]3.[H+]4 >> [_A]1[O+]2([H]3)([H]4)) is the CI protonation that forms the R-OH2(+) precursor ion (also correct); it is referenced here as the ion-forming step but is not encoded as a formal_arrow_step in this record (0 arcs drawn; mapped H not trackable in the RDKit-parsed SMILES). The rule maps both hydrogens explicitly; this record carries them as implicit H on oxygen, which is connectivity-equivalent.
